subject: data
text:
| Data type | Strategy | Lifecycle |
|-----------|----------|-----------|
| On-disk product state (`events.ndjson`, `snapshot.json`, `heartbeat`, `plugin/`, `settings.json`) | Produced only by running real `viola run` / `hook` / CLI verbs against `viola-fake-agent` in a fresh home, never hand-written. Two exceptions: the chaos tests, which corrupt files the product already wrote; and on Windows x64 the root tests' `seed_conpty`, which hard-links (or copies) the ConPTY companions into `<home>/bin/<key>/conpty/`, byte-identical to what viola would write (§5 carve-out; `conpty_sideload` never seeds, so it covers the product's write). A home that seed made is not one viola created, and a first boot and stop does not change that: `hook statusline`'s instance check refuses it (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, CI run 38080061631, three cases; the refused home's DACL was not read, and that reading is owed to the working-route entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity"). A case that needs a home viola created on every OS starts from `stamped_home`, as the every-OS `hook_statusline` cases that run the arm's whole course do. | per-test fresh (TempDir) |

subject: data-fake-agent
text:
- Modes: `--suppress-prompt-submit`, `--local-command-mode` (a `/`-prefixed prompt fires no UserPromptSubmit), `--inject-harness-turn` (one gated step before the script that fires a `<task-notification>`-prefixed prompt with `origin:"harness"`), `--exit-no-eof` (a bounded re-exec holder keeps the child's console / PTY slave open for 10 s — not viola's stdout — writes a `hold` receipt, and on Unix spawns in its own process group), `--report-version <ver>`, print mode `-p <prompt>` / `--print <prompt>` (it writes its start receipts, fires SessionStart/default, UserPromptSubmit/default with `prompt` set, Stop/default and SessionEnd/default from the fixture set, prints `ok` on stdout and exits 0; never raw, never reading stdin — the mode `viola verify`'s print probe drives against the fake agent in CI; `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` is 2.1.287, the recorded set's version, so the default `--version` answer is `2.1.287 (Claude Code)`, and the harness's `viola_e2e::harness::boot::DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` — the `boot --cli-version` default — is the same), thirteen argv options (no env; the count's rule is architecture's list of them), two of them for the statusline tests, `--settings <file>` and `--statusline-stdin <file>` (the settings command runs with both options, only when it is absolute, with the stdin file's bytes on its stdin, and under `--framing` without `--statusline-stdin` with the set's recorded `StatusLine` variants), and the eleven that follow, nine of them for verify's interactive runs and their tests
 — `--trusted-root <DIR>` (an ancestor walk, both paths canonicalised), `--screens` (writes `Screen.modal` when untrusted, no hook fired, or `Screen.ready` when trusted, SessionStart as before: a clear, then rows joined by CRLF) , `--turn-stop` (a submit fires UserPromptSubmit, then Stop, then writes `Screen.turn`), `--dialogs` (Runs C and D: a pasted compiled dialog prompt replays its recorded `<stem>-<n>` variants in claim order — a call's PreToolUse first; with no decision its PermissionRequest; a decision from either fires its PostToolUse), `--framing` (Run B: a pasted compiled paste text fires its recorded `paste-1` / `paste-2` / `paste-3` UserPromptSubmit variant with its bytes unchanged, a new stem reached through `ledger::framing_stem` with no option added, the probed `/clear` fires the recorded `clear-1` SessionEnd then SessionStart and no UserPromptSubmit, and the probed `/compact` the recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id` and no UserPromptSubmit; and, with an absolute `--settings` status line command, the set's `StatusLine.default-1.json` after the launch SessionStart and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` once after the first Stop; a set without a variant fires nothing for it, and without the option the agent echoes the typed text) and the two test-only holds `--stop-receipt-hold-ms <n>` (capped at 1 000 ms, a hold of the Stop hook's receipt that forces a race window open; `fire` reports whether a hook printed) and `--paste-hint-ms <ms>` (capped at 10 000 ms;
 with `--framing`, after the long text's replay and its Stop the screen is cleared and `Screen.turn` is drawn only after the hold, which forces open the window in which a real CLI shows its paste hint) and the test-only screen switch `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: after the turn of the compiled tag-like paste, and after no other turn, the agent draws `Screen.<phase>.json` of its set in place of `Screen.turn`; a missing file draws nothing), the test-only screen switch `--long-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: after the long paste's turn alone, after its Stop, the agent draws `Screen.<phase>.json` of its set in place of `Screen.turn`; parse cases `opts_long_turn_screen_takes_the_phase_it_names_alone` and `opts_long_turn_screen_defaults_to_none`), and two for `viola revive`'s tests and, under the fake agent, verify's Run E, `--resume <id>` (the launch SessionStart reports source `resume` and that id) and `--fork-session` (beside `--resume`, the compiled fork id; alone it changes nothing); every wrapper boot in `tests/support` and the harness passes `--screens --trusted-root <cwd>` (`Wrapper::boot_untrusted` passes no root), and a test whose fake agent writes another screen (e.g. `--vt100-panic-bytes`) keeps its own verdict — and unknown arguments ignored. Beside the options the agent takes two mode words. `statusline-echo`, landed at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through: it prints its output and files its stdin, and its exit is the code after the marker path.
 `agents` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json`, and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry: a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, its `cwd` the launch fixture's recorded `cwd`, `~` without one; a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env are added; units `agents_output_*`, `live_sessions_skip_a_dead_or_reused_pid`, `launch_session_replays_the_recorded_id_and_cwd` and `planted_rows_of_a_malformed_rows_file_are_none`. The `--resume` launch payload is recorded since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows: Run E recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` live on 2.1.287, and the launch builds on it there; the rewritten default payload stays only for a set without the variant. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, a live reading on `claude` 2.1.287 holds 10 key names where the rewritten payload holds 5 (`cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `session_id`, `source`, `transcript_path`; the five more are `context_tokens`, `estimated_cache_write_usd`, `prompt_cache_likely_expired`, `scratchpad_dir`, `seconds_since_last_response`; as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, `evidence/live-revive.md`). The recorded variant holds those 10 key names, and the `--resume` shape is the `resume-session` ledger row. `--vt100-panic-bytes` is built (with confirmed `send`'s chaos case): after its `start` receipt it writes `e4 b8 ad` once to its terminal and receipts nothing new. Its bytes are measured: under a 24×1 PTY a wide character (`e4 b8 ad`) panics vt100 0.16.2, so no new env seam is needed (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants). `--report-version` changes only the `--version` answer.
 Fixture replay still follows `--cli-version` / `--fixtures`, so a home stamped for a fixture version can run an unlisted reported version (Path 7).

subject: mocking
text: - Time: sync crates use mock_instant 0.6.1 (global mode) or the injected `viola_core::Clock` for heartbeat 1 s / 5 s and the send confirmation window. `budget_override_until` is no clock-seam case: the budget gate's decision takes `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` as an argument, and its expiry is a pure-function unit case (§4, chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor). Async crates (`viola-mcp`) use `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` from tokio 1.53.3 `test-util` for any timer the MCP adapter itself owns. The `wait` `timeout_ms` deadline runs in the wrapper process, and only the injected `viola_core::Clock` in the §4 root-bin case drives it. A paused tokio clock in a test never reaches a spawned wrapper (§11 Universal). `chrono::Utc::now()` is read only through the clock seam, with one exception as landed: the budget gate's three evaluation points read it directly and hand the instant to the pure decision (as read in `src/run/send.rs` and `src/cmd/run.rs` at the chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor wrap; that read named the gate's call sites only and was no census of `Utc::now()`).

subject: ci
text:
- **Stage:** Lint
  - **Runs:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent -- -D warnings`; `cargo check` with one `-p` per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` (no `--features`, so no tokio; target set `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, four since `viola-channel` left the list at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers — its Tokio client sits behind its `tokio` feature and its normal graph is held by the tree form `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`, Supply-chain row — each joining the list with its crate; an empty list fails; job `lint`); `bash scripts/orphans-check.sh --probe && bash scripts/orphans-check.sh` (cargo-modules 0.27.0: `cargo modules orphans -p <pkg> {--lib | --bin <name>} [--features <required features>] --deny` for every lib/bin target from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, last line `orphans-check: N/N targets clean`; the probe fires on each of its two planted orphans, last line `orphans-check probes: 2/2 fired, control clean`). `cargo modules dependencies --acyclic` is an on-demand boundary review, not a gate: at cargo-modules 0.27.0 every type and its own inherent method read as a cycle whatever the filters (measured at chunk 2026-09-24-workspace-tree-and-code-graph-planes, 3 of 4 targets). The rmcp release-graph assertion is the lint step `rmcp features (exactly server + transport-io, non-vacuous)` (every OS, after `Lint probes`; chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): `bash scripts/rmcp-features.sh` runs `cargo tree -e features -p viola --edges normal --target all -i rmcp --no-dedupe --prefix depth`, rmcp must be present and the features a non-rmcp package requests exactly `server transport-io`, last line `rmcp-features: server transport-io`.
 Beside CI, a chunk plan may list a check-only Windows-target clippy as a chunk gate entry on the Linux dev host, which does not build the `cfg(windows)` code CI lints (first listed by chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-cleanup; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/wincheck cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features fake-agent --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings`, nothing linked, the target std installed as host preparation): neither a CI step nor a `pre-push` stage.
  - **Parallel:** per OS matrix
  - **Cache:** Swatinem/rust-cache v2.9.2 (SHA-pinned; key: OS + toolchain + `Cargo.lock`), in `ci.yml` only

subject: gate-mutation
text:
**Mutation gate (Founder Direction 1):** judged at the epoch boundary by `/andromeda-code-audit` and on demand by `run --mutants`; no chunk, pre-push or CI mutation gate exists since 2026-09-28 (the founder's ruling, 17:59). `mutants.out/outcomes.json` for the diff (the run's own output: under the host mutation scratch on a Windows host, §3 `run` step 4) must show `missed == 0`, `timeout == 0` and `unviable <= caught`, where `missed` reads after the harness has left out the host-excluded records (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). `unviable` mutants are reported, and a few do not fail the gate. When they outnumber the caught ones the run is red (`unviable-exceeds-caught`), because a run whose mutant builds mostly failed is no evidence of test strength. The threshold was picked by measurement across every CI leg with an uploaded verdict while the legs existed (2026-09-25). Healthy legs had unviable/caught ≤ 0.044 (chunk 7: 3/114 and 3/113; this cleanup: 4/139, 4/139, and 6/137 on the dev host). The failed windows leg of run 36118112104 had 135/8. A diff that names no `.rs` path (docs, specs, fixtures) never reaches cargo-mutants: it passes with the explicit `"mutants":{"tested":0,"verdict":"no-rust-delta","diff":"target/agent-run/chunk.diff","files":N}`. A diff whose `.rs` paths are all test targets (`tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, at the root or under `crates/<member>/`) has nothing cargo-mutants can mutate: it passes only with the explicit `test-only-rust-delta` verdict, which names the diff, its file count and `rust_files`. Any other diff naming a `.rs` path, a mixed one included, is `counted`, and a counted run that produces no fresh `outcomes.json` is red. A mutant caught only by a doctest counts as missed under nextest, so the missing unit test must be added.
 The boundary tier scores a whole member with `run --mutants --package <member>` (viola-e2e: `run --mutants --package viola-e2e`, its verdict `package`) under the same `missed == 0`, `timeout == 0`, `unviable <= caught`. A mutant this host cannot compile or reach — inside a `cfg(windows)` item or block, or behind a const such as `HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)` — is recorded "not measured here; owed to {the route entry that measures it}" by coordinate, never "equivalent", and never counted as caught; `missed == 0` then reads over the measurable set (the overseer's ruling, 2026-10-04). Since chunk 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade the harness applies the first case itself: a missed mutant whose whole span sits under a `cfg` attribute proved false for the host is left out of the count and named with its predicate in the document's `mutants.host_excluded` (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). A mutant behind a const compiles on both hosts, is never left out, and stays a record by coordinate. The first whole-member `viola-e2e` score on the Linux dev host read 718 mutants in 5356 s (89 min 16 s): 656 caught, 2 missed, 0 timeout, 60 unviable, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup-ii/evidence/e2e-score.md`. Its 2 missed are in `prepare` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs`). `prepare` takes its host flag from `mutate()` (`scratch::HOST_SCRATCH`), so both arms are reached on every host, and both mutants (`Ok(None)` and the deleted `!`) read killed on the Linux dev host by its scratch case (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`). The route entry "Windows mutation grade" measured them: both read caught on `windows-2025` (run 38036448183, job `mutants (viola-e2e)`).
 The Epoch 4 boundary audit's Linux whole-member runs read 47 missed (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-12T06-54-29-code-audit/record.json`, `mutation.survivors`); chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors disposed each in its ledger `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors/evidence/survivors.ndjson`: 29 by a nextest case in the package that owns the mutated file, 7 of them after a behaviour-preserving restatement that made the site reachable on Linux (`viola_state::fs`'s retry decision passed in by the caller, `viola send`'s issue-line decision a named function), each shown red under its hand-applied mutant and green restored with no mutation run made; the 2 `prepare` rows above stood as recorded (killed on every host since, above); and the 16 in `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (whose code now sits under its children in `src/cmd/verify/typed/`; `framing_turns` 5, `SharedPty` 5, `Run`'s ending sequence 6) were disposed by chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii in its ledger `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`, each after a behaviour-preserving restatement inside that module (the two framing waits the named predicates `added_turn_ended` and `local_command_answered`, every `clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE` the one function `probe_until`, `SharedPty` generic over its `Pty` and reached through a test-only recording double, the Ctrl-C ending and the pump wait the plain functions `ctrl_c_ending` and `ended_by`) and a case in its unit tests, each shown red under its hand-applied mutant and green restored with no mutation run made; none is owed. The Epoch 5 boundary audit's own run is the reader that confirms the 45 kills (the 29 of chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors and the 16 of chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii).
 The Epoch 5 boundary audit's 16 survivors were each disposed by a nextest case in the package that owns the mutated file, 10 killed and 6 after a behaviour-preserving restatement, each red under its hand-applied mutant and green reverted byte-exact, with no mutation run made and none equivalent or recorded (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`). The boundary audit measures the `cfg(windows)` code by dispatching `windows-mutants.yml` (founder ruling C2, 2026-10-04; §9 Mutation row): `run --mutants --package <member> --file …` per matrix item on `windows-2025` (§9 Mutation row), verdict `package`, report-only and never a gate. In its first run, 37174673472, 19 of 25 misses were `#[cfg(unix)]` twins in the scoped files, which the Windows build compiles out and cargo-mutants grades missed, with 0 timeouts across 508 mutants (`viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-04-windows-boundary-mutation-workflow/evidence/windows-dispatch.md`). The harness now leaves such twins out itself (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). Run 38036448183 read all nine jobs green over 642 mutants: 537 caught, 75 unviable, 30 left out as host-excluded (the sum of the nine documents' `host_excluded` lengths), 0 missed and 0 timeout, the longest job 49 min against the 120 min ceiling, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade/evidence/windows-dispatch.md`. That run was one dispatch outside the boundary audit, made on 2026-10-10 for chunk 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade alone and on the founder's own word for it; the ruling stands as written.
 On the Linux dev host every mutation run takes `TMPDIR=<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`, a NOCOW (`chattr +C`) btrfs dir set by the operator (an environment fact; the harness's scratch arm stays Windows-only): cargo-mutants 27.1.0 copies the tree, `target/` included, into the temp dir; `/tmp` there is a 32 GB `usrquota` tmpfs that a full viola-e2e run overflowed at 460/709; and on a COW btrfs dir its reflink copy drops the exec bit of the prebuilt `viola-fake-agent` (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion/evidence/m3.md`). The Epoch 4 audit ran two cargo-mutants jobs (`-j 2`) under one such `TMPDIR` and read viola-pty's `PortablePty::resize` → `Ok(())` missed, while its three resize tests, run alone under that mutant, read red (as measured at chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors, `evidence/survivors.md`); that the other job's unmutated run wrote the awaited `size 120x40` line into the report file both shared is recorded, not established (the two-job run was not re-run). The report files now carry the test process's id (architecture §Occupied Resources), so two jobs never share one. The two real-cargo-mutants harness tests (`run_mutants_passes_when_the_change_is_tested`, `run_mutants_reports_survivors_of_an_untested_change`) are compiled out on macOS (`#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`, never `#[ignore]`): there cargo-mutants' baseline build in its copied tree takes ~77 s of an 80.9 s phase against 0.41 s for the same cold build outside it, with no first-launch or jobserver cost, as measured at CI run 36481260151 (the chunk 2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary's `evidence/macos-mutants-phases.md`); the cause inside that phase stays unnamed, so under the operator's ruling it is runner-side. Both run on ubuntu and windows; `[profile.ci]`'s 120 s kill and `retries = 0` are unchanged.

subject: gate-perf
text: - **Perf session:** `--perf` then boots ONE session through its `PerfSession` seam (`boot::boot` / `cleanup::cleanup`; the harness's own tests stand in for both): `perf-<harness pid>`, a `builder` instance, `BootOptions { bin_dir: target/perf/release, build: false, stamp: false }`, its home under `target/e2e-home/` (boot step 2), unstamped, so the `pre-tool-use` row times the unverified-CLI path (`hook.dialog` → `null` at once). Each row's synthetic payload (string fields only, the tests-owned content canary in content fields; no recorded fixture exists yet) is written to `target/agent-run/<session>/payload-<hook>.json` and fed through `--input`; hyperfine runs with the repo root as cwd and `VIOLA_NAME=builder` / `VIOLA_DIR=<perf home>/instances/builder` set, so every timed hook takes the real logging and channel path, never the no-instance no-op (obs-plan §10 obs-overhead row) — as measured at chunk 2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate: a kept-home run held 132 `hook-decision` lines with no fallback `detail` and 33 wrapper events per row. Each row's stale export is removed first. After the last row and **before** `cleanup`, `--perf` asserts the home's role files (`diagnostics/*.ndjson` without `detail-*`) hold no `event:"panic"` line, with no seam exemption, because a hook panic exits 0 and hyperfine cannot see it; a panic line fails `panic`. Then `cleanup` (`keep_homes` = `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` exactly `1`) must report `ok:true`. A failed build (`build`), boot (`boot: <reason>`), row (the hook's name), panic check or cleanup turns suite `perf` red with the failure named, never a missing or skipped row.
